name: Bullet-pattern emitter
oneLiner: Enemies cast bullet patterns described as data: fans and aimed bursts, rings, spirals, flowers whose speed dips between petals, weaving waves, curtain walls with a moving gap, big orbs that burst into rings, curving and falling shots, each with speed, acceleration and turn curves. Every bullet comes from a fixed pool (no garbage per frame), is drawn in code with a bright white core, a coloured body and rim, a dark outline and a soft halo, readable on light and dark floors, crisp at any dpr or as whole game pixels, and hits with a circle far smaller than it looks (swept, so fast bullets never tunnel). Grazes are reported, walls stop bullets, a dying caster's bullets fade into sparks. The game keeps its rules: it gives the player's hit circle and applies damage in onHit. A safeGap() analysis sweeps the band the player can reach and reports whether a gap at least the player's hit circle stays open and reachable at every step.
fits: top-down action RPG (enemies and bosses that cast)
side-scrolling action and platformers (turrets, casters, falling rain)
boss fights in any real-time 2D game
any 2D canvas game, pixel or HD
notFor: turn-based battles with no real-time movement (nothing to dodge)
physics projectiles that bounce, stick or collide with each other (bullets only fly, split and stop at walls)
player weapons with ammo, reload and spread logic (this is the enemy side; the same module can fire player shots but has no weapon rules)

needs: a fixed update step that calls update(dt) once per step after movement (also run by ?t= fast-forward and ?auto=1), update(0) while paused, in hit-stop or behind a window
the player's small hit circle in world px (player(): {x, y, r} or null), and canHit() for invulnerability
the game's own damage function, called from onHit(hit)
per caster an id and a source (world px, or null when dead / off-scene); enemy death to cancel and stop it
the draw pass: one call after the sprites, before the HUD, with the camera offset; clear() on new game, restart and every scene switch
provides: bullet patterns as data: fan, ring, spiral, aimed, flower, wave, line, layers, split into sub-patterns, speed / accel / turn curves, gravity
pooled bullets, swept hit tests with a hit circle smaller than the drawn bullet, grazes, walls, bullet cancel into sparks
drawing: core, body, rim, outline, halo; muzzle flash, hit pop, graze sparks; smooth (device px) or pixel render
safeGap(pattern, opts): passable / reachable verdict with the narrowest gap
danger(x, y, r, aheadMs) for autopilots; stats(), list(), hash() for tests and judges

assets: module/bullet-patterns.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_Bullets): pattern normaliser and presets, fixed bullet / effect / burst pools, casters, integration with speed / accel / turn curves, gravity and sine weave, sub-pattern splits, swept hit and graze tests, walls, cancel, code-drawn sprites cached per colour, size and angle at device resolution (or game pixels), safeGap() analysis, danger() query
no image, font or audio files
